summary: The root نَسْلَ (nasala) is used in an imprecation, similar to saying "woe to him" or "may he stumble." It implies a curse or a wish for misfortune upon someone.
lane: نَسْلًَا وَأَسْلًا ذ is a form of imprecation against a man, like تَعْسًا وَنَكْسًا . (M, in art. اسل .)

headwords.def: said of camels' fur: see عَصِيمٌ.

Progeny, whether of man or beast. (The Lexicons passim.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
